plan.title: Add draft, commit and submit states to bh's inputs and forms
plan.description: Every form has three states. The draft: what you're typing, local to the field. Committed: the field has handed it over, on Enter, on leaving the field or the window, or after a pause in typing. Submitted: the form has sent it, on Save, or at each commit when the form saves as you go. Today bh's controls report every keystroke, so committing is each caller's: tickets' `BlurCommitInput` (`apps/web/src/registry/field-widget.tsx:19`, leaving only, no Enter or Escape, remounted with a `key` at `:100` to take a change made elsewhere), its number field's wrapper (`:116`) and `InlineTitle` (`components/item-detail.tsx`), icon-editor's `ColourPairField`, session-board's `SessionTitle`. `@bh/form` knows only submit (`onSubmit`; validation on blur and on submit). No new component: a `commit` prop on the text controls and `onCommit` beside `onSubmit` in `@bh/form`.

subtickets.title: Add `useInlineEdit`, the draft behind the prop
subtickets.description: `useInlineEdit({ value, onCommit, commit })` holds the draft and gives its handlers. It commits only a changed value; while the field isn't being edited it follows a new `value` from outside (no remount); Escape puts the committed value back. A pending pause commits at once when you leave or the field unmounts, so a draft is never lost. It stays inside bh, not exported, until a caller that isn't one of the controls needs it. `useParsedDraft` (TK-28) is the same with a parse step: build one on the other.

subtickets.title: Add `commit` to `Input`, `Textarea` and `NumberInput`
subtickets.description: `commit`: `'change'`, the default, commits every keystroke as today; `'leave'` commits on Enter, on leaving the field and on leaving the window; `{ after: 800 }` does that and also commits after 800 ms without typing. `Textarea`: Enter stays a new line. `NumberInput`: leaving the whole control commits, and a run of stepper clicks commits once. `SearchInput` and `PasswordInput` pass it to `Input`. A form or table config sets it per field as data (`{ commit: 'leave' }`).

blockedBy.why: the `commit` prop runs on `useInlineEdit`'s draft

subtickets.title: Write the controls' tests and docs
subtickets.description: Each trigger on each of the three: Enter, leaving the field, leaving the window, the pause; nothing for an unchanged value; Escape reverting; an outside change replacing the draft while idle but not while typing; a pending pause committed on leaving. The contract says a control holds no value of its own (`inputs/contract.ts`); it gets the exception: with `commit` other than `'change'` it holds a draft while you edit. A `commit` demo on each control's docs page, with the callers' cases: a field, a title, a "+ add" input.

subtickets.title: Add `onCommit` beside `onSubmit` in `@bh/form`
subtickets.description: The form has two outputs. `onCommit(change, values)` runs each time a field commits, with what changed (`{ field, value, previous }`) and the form's values after it; `onSubmit(values)` runs on Save, as today. A form uses either or both: tickets' item detail saves each field as it commits (one PATCH each) and has no Save; a create dialog sends everything on Save; a settings page can check a field as it commits and save on Save. `onCommit` may return a promise: while it runs the field shows it's saving, and if it fails the field keeps your value and shows the error. The form's values are committed values: a field's draft joins them when it commits. `commit` (when a field commits) is set per form, overridable per field, and passed to the control. Dirty means committed but not submitted: it drives "Unsaved changes", the Save button and a warning on leaving the page, so a form with no `onSubmit` is never dirty. Save while typing commits the draft first, so it isn't lost. Tests for each, and a docs page that shows a field's draft, committed and submitted values side by side as you type.

subtickets.title: Fold a form's visible field values into `{ search, filter }`
subtickets.description:
`foldFilter(nodes, values): { search?: string; filter: Filter }` in `src/filter/fold.ts`. The field named `search` becomes `search`, left out when `''`. Each field with a `filter` (TK-75.3) writes into one `{ all: [...] }`:

- `{ op }`: `{ field, op, value }`, unless the value is its kind's empty one (`''`, `null`, `[]`, `false`) or `map` turns it to `null`. An operator that takes no operand (`empty`, `notEmpty`, `isMe`: its `OperatorSpec` has no `operand`) writes `{ field, op }` while the value isn't empty.
- `{ range }`: up to two conditions, one per half that's set.
- `{ presets }`: the filter of each preset that's on; an `all` is spread into the list, anything else is one entry.
- `{ rules }`: each entry as it is.

The same condition, deep-equal, is written once. It folds the values it's given, so a field hidden by `when` writes nothing when given the visible values, as `onCommit` and `onSubmit` hand them. Unit tests for each shape, and for the seven apps' `FormConfig`s on the design's canvas.

When a field's new value no longer writes a condition its old value wrote, every other field holding that condition lets it go: a preset turns off, an `{ op }` field takes its empty value, and the `rules` list loses it. So removing a condition from one field removes it from all (the user's answer on TK-75). The design's case: unpicking Blocked in the status chips turns a "Blocked" preset off too. epics.title: Add one resource API for every app

features.title: Write the resource contract
features.description:
What every endpoint answers to (lists, edits and actions), and the metadata that describes its fields. Its plan's types follow what's chosen below.

```http
GET    /api/<resource>/meta                → ResourceMeta     TK-11.1
POST   /api/<resource>/query    Query      → QueryResult      TK-11.2
GET    /api/<resource>/:id                 → Row              TK-11.3
POST   /api/<resource>          Create     → 201 Row          TK-11.3
PATCH  /api/<resource>/:id      Patch      → Row              TK-11.3
DELETE /api/<resource>/:id?version=…       → 204              TK-11.3
POST   /api/<resource>/:id/actions/<name>  ActionInput → ActionResult  TK-11.7
any of them, on an error                   → ErrorBody        TK-11.4
```

Every type named on this page is defined on it, in the ticket that brings it in.
features.statusNote: TK-11.1 is on bh's main. On bh branch `tk-11`, in `../bh-wt-tk-11`, moved up to bh's main (b909d45), not merged, all in `@bh/resource` (`packages/shared/resource`): TK-11.2.2 (6b483a0) the operator registry, `OperatorSpec` and `baseOperators`, bh's twelve as its entries, each kind naming its operators in `baseKinds` (TK-11.1's `BaseOperator` union and table are gone), and `createKindRegistry` refusing a kind that names an unregistered operator; TK-11.8 (fcee60a) a url value may be a path from the root, `//host` and relative paths refused; TK-11.2.6 (8e0e770) search and fields; TK-11.2.1 (5756aaa) the filter tree; TK-11.2.3 (9b99407) sort, `ResourceMeta.sort` required; TK-11.2.4 (87391dd) paging in two shapes that can't be mixed, `PageResult {next, total}`; TK-11.2.5 (129b3a7) grouping with `all`; TK-11.4 (105b2cd) `ErrorBody`, generic over its codes, and `issuesOf` flattening valibot's issues; TK-11.3 (9ff8ff8) `Create` and `Patch` with `version`. 114 package tests; bh's typecheck, lint and build pass. Choices: `contains`/`startsWith` on a many field hold when any value matches; ranges compare datetimes by instant. Left for TK-11.5: the valibot schemas, `matchesFilter`, `createRegistry`, JSON Schema and OpenAPI; nothing gives a sort comparator in JS yet, which a client re-placing a written row (TK-12.3) would need. TK-11.7 (94a7ef3) actions: `ResourceMeta.actions` (`ActionMeta {name, label, on: 'row' | 'resource', input: FieldMeta[], long}`), an action answering its row (200), nothing on the whole resource (204), or a `{job}` when it runs long (202); `Job` queued, running, then done (with the row) or failed (with an `ErrorBody` error); `GET /api/jobs/:id` answers the job whatever its status, 404 for an unknown one. A query pages by skip and take by default, and by cursor as an option: every answer carries the next page's cursor, and a query may pass it back instead of `skip` (your answer: "skip/take default cursor as an option").

A stored definition (a resource's fields, a view, a template) holds no logic: field paths, text templates, filter trees and the names of renderers and formatters registered in code; a computed value such as "days open" is a field the server computes, so it filters and sorts like any other (your answer).

A field's metadata says how its value shows with a `format` (bytes, duration, percent, money…), and bh has a default renderer per kind (an option as a pill in its color, a user as an avatar and name), so a field shows the same everywhere unless a template says otherwise (your answer).
A resource's metadata names it in the singular and the plural, `label: {one: 'Item', other: 'Items'}`, so buttons, questions and counts read right from the metadata (your answer).

A field's `format` names an entry of bh's format registry, never one of a fixed list in the contract, so an app adds a format by registering it (your note on TK-11.1: "I want it to be read from format registries").

A field's kind is a name in a kind registry, as its format is, never one of a fixed set of types: bh registers nine, an app adds its own, and a field is one shape whose kind-specific `settings` its kind checks (your note on TK-11.1: "those must be also from registries so I can easily add new field type").

A row's picture is a url template, `image?: Template`: `'{photo}'` when a field holds the address, `'/api/users/{id}/avatar'` when it's built from fields; each placeholder URL-encoded, an empty one meaning no picture (your answer).

A field may be declared with a template over the row's other fields (`{key: 'name', kind: 'text', template: '{project}-{number} {title}'}`); the server fills it in every row, and `ResourceMeta.titleField` and `imageField` name a field (your answer).
A field that points at rows of another resource has one general kind, `ref`, whose `settings.of` names that resource (`users`, `items`, `projects`), and the `user` kind goes (your answer).
`ResourceMeta`'s keys that name a field end in `Field`: `idField`, `titleField`, `imageField` and `versionField` (your note on TK-11.1: "it must be titleField, imageField").

The metadata groups its keys: `ResourceMeta.roles` holds `idField`, `titleField`, `imageField` and `versionField`, and `FieldMeta` is `{key, label, type: {kind, settings?, many?}, format?, template?, query, write}`, with `default` in `write` (your answer).

The query groups its paging: `page: {skip?, take?} | {cursor, take?}`, two shapes that never mix; the answer is `{rows, groups?, page: {next, total}}` (your answer, from your note on TK-11.2: "skip/take and cursor/total shouldn't be used together").

A filter's operators are a registry, as kinds and formats are: `Registry.operators` holds `OperatorSpec`s (name, label, operand schema); bh registers its twelve, `KindSpec.operators` names registered ones, and an app adds its own with its SQL and filter input (your answer).

`filter` and `search` sit directly in `Query`: `{filter?, search?, sort?, page?, group?, fields?}`, without a `where` group (your answer, from your note on TK-11.2: "filter and search should be in query").
A `url` value is absolute, with its scheme, or a path from the root (`/api/users/7/avatar`), which a client resolves against the API's address (your answer).

A filter operator's JavaScript check, `matches(value, operand)`, is on its registry entry in `@bh/resource`; each adapter keeps its SQL in a table by operator name, bh's twelve built in and an app adding its own, and a server refuses to start when the registry holds an operator its adapter has no SQL for (your answer).
Every page answers the total, numbered or not: a query has no `total` flag (your note on TK-11.2.4).
Grouping keeps its `all` flag: a query asks for the groups no row holds when it needs them, as a board's empty columns (your answer).

notes.text: It guards against two people overwriting each other. When you open an item, the client also reads its version: the value of the field the resource names for that (`roles.versionField`), for items `updatedAt`. When you save, the client sends that value back as `version`. If someone saved the item in between, its `updatedAt` has moved on, so the server answers 409 `conflict` and writes nothing, and the client can show the newer item instead of silently replacing it. notes.text:
From the builder, after TK-29.1 to TK-29.4 (built on bh branch `tk-29`, not merged): the choices its worker made, for you to see (say so in a note to change one).

- While an async `onConfirm` runs, nothing closes the dialog, not Esc, Cancel or the dim: the work can't be called back, so the dialog stays to show how it went.
- `onConfirm` returns `unknown`, so handlers that return a number still compile and `onConfirm={() => mutation.mutateAsync(id)}` works as it is.
- `useConfirm` needs one `ConfirmProvider` around the app, as `ToastProvider` does; asks are answered one at a time, and focus goes back to what asked. A dialog's `children` then render inside the provider, seeing its context, not the caller's; the docs say to use `ConfirmDialog` directly when that matters.
- A typed phrase must match exactly; medialib's own ignores case and spaces, so its move (TK-70.2.2) changes that.

Also placed: the release that carries it is TK-38.3 (with `Kbd`), tickets' update TK-38.4, which TK-5.19 now waits on; two follow-ups are new TK-106 (the provider in `AppShell`, a busy flag for the body); and each app's move says what its dialog becomes.

chosen: The shared hooks live in a new small package, `@bh/hooks`, below `@bh/table` and `@bh/shell` (and `@bh/ui`), which import it (your answer).
Every shared hook follows one shape, designed first: options in; state, actions and prop getters out; no markup; with one layout for its tests and docs page (your answer).
A shared hook takes one options object, except a hook about a single value takes that value first: `useMediaQuery(query)`, `useDebouncedValue(value, { delay })` (your answer).
`usePersistedState` returns a pair, `[value, setValue]`, as `useState` does, under the rule that a hook standing in for one of React's returns what React's does (your answer).
`@bh/hooks` exports `useControllableState`, the shared logic for a value either controlled by the caller (`value`, `onChange`) or held by the component (`defaultValue`) (your answer).
Two places using `usePersistedState` with the same key stay in step, on the page and across the app's open tabs, through the browser's `storage` event (your answer).
bh's lint checks React hooks (`eslint-plugin-react-hooks` 7: the rules of hooks, exhaustive deps, the React Compiler's ref and purity checks) for `@bh/hooks` only, for now (your answer).
`useDisclosure`'s trigger is a `<button>` only; its getter sets `type="button"` (your answer).

When a hook's prop getter (`getTriggerProps({ onClick })`) merges the caller's handler with its own, both run, the caller's first and then the hook's; the caller can't stop the hook's own handling. Built so in `@bh/hooks`' `mergeProps` (bh 0.6.0) (your answer).

A shared hook hands over an element's props through prop getters (`getTriggerProps(own?)`, `getRegionProps(own?)`, `getHandleProps(own?)`, `getSeparatorProps(own?)`), which merge the caller's own props, handlers and ref into the hook's, not through plain prop objects the caller merges by hand. Built so in bh 0.6.0: `useDisclosure`, `useDrag` and `useResizeHandle` return getters, and `usePanelWidth` returns `getSeparatorProps()` (your answer).

From the builder: TK-32.2 (`formatDateTime`) and TK-32.3 (the `locale` option) are built on bh branch `tk-32`, not merged; TK-32.1 (minute and hour steps) still waits on TK-31.5, `useNow`. **New TK-32.4**, the release, and **TK-32.5**, tickets' update to it, which TK-5.16 (tickets' dates) now waits on.

The choices its worker made, for you to see (say so in a note to change one):

- `formatDateTime` uses the reader's own time zone, not UTC as bh's day helpers do: a time of day in UTC is wrong for most readers, and cv, gateway, items-core, wallet-passes and bh's `DateColumn` already use local time. `timeZone: 'UTC'` or an IANA zone sets it; an unknown zone falls back to the reader's rather than throwing.
- Without a locale, the clock is 24-hour in fixed English (`Jul 13, 2026, 09:05`), as `formatExact`, `TimePicker` and four apps write it. With a locale, the clock is that locale's own, so `locale: 'en-US'` gives `2:30 PM`, not the same as no locale; the docs say so.
- Without a locale, `formatExact`, `relativeLabel` and `RelativeDate` write exactly what they wrote before.
- The docs are on `RelativeDate`'s page, since bh's docs site files `@bh/ui` pages only under components.

Found: Georgian. A browser without Georgian locale data (the Chrome the docs check ran in has none) writes `locale: 'ka'` in English, with no error; wallet-passes' own formatters do the same today. bh can't fix that without a translation layer, which your answer ruled out; the docs warn about it.

plan.title: Merge `bbendeliani/detection` into items-core's main
plan.description:
A worker merges items-core's `bbendeliani/detection` into its main and pushes it only if the merge's checks pass; if any fail it pushes nothing and tells you (your answer on TK-66). `@bh/config` and the `node-file-suffix` rule, which TK-66.2 needs, exist only on that branch.

It waits on no cloud cutover any more: Google Cloud is dropped (your words, 2026-10-16), and while `bnw-items-dev`'s billing is off a push to items-core's main deploys nothing there. items-core deploys to the gateway instead (IC/E4): its stack deploys `main` on each push once it exists (IC-18.2). Whichever comes first: if the stack exists with deploy on push before this push, the push is its first deploy (IC-18.4); otherwise IC-18.4 deploys `main` by hand after it. The stack's compose file, the gateway's docs and the fixture crawl's new baseline are built on main after this merge (IC-17, IC-19, IC-20.5). The branch's later migrations drop columns and tables; on the gateway, whose database starts empty, rolling back past them is a restore from the shared Postgres's nightly dump or a reset (IC-19.1).

Done 2026-10-16: merged as `7776b1e1` and pushed to items-core's main (`b1ccebf8..7776b1e1`, 265 commits). Its checks passed in Docker on the database's network, on Node 24 with Playwright's Chromium: typecheck, lint and every test, 125 of 125 turbo tasks, with the isolated database suites run against `items_test`. Four suites stay skipped as designed: they need a browser over CDP, a live Nike capture, a worker-role setup, or `CRAWLER_BROWSER_TEST` passed through turbo. Nothing deployed: Cloud Build can't run with billing off, and the gateway has no items-core stack yet.

epics.title: Make tickets the task system: the plans, their screens and their agents
epics.description:
The tickets app becomes the task system: the plans in `tasks/*.json` move into its database, the viewer's screens are rebuilt in it on bh's views, and the planner and builder work through its MCP tools. That is your answer to the direction question, under TK-80 (2026-10-12), and the plan follows it.

How the two compare, read from the code on 2026-10-12:

- **Data**: tasks/ has four fixed levels and ids that say where an item sits (`TK-11.2.1`); tickets has typed items in a scheme, a parent per item, fields of eight kinds, and keys made of a prefix and a number. Close: the plans fit a scheme of their own (TK-80.1), their ids need a stored key (TK-80.3), and GW is a prefix on both sides (TK-85).
- **State**: both have a status, with done and dropped kinds. Only tasks/ has approval as the gate to build, blockers with a why that children inherit, waits in words, `where`, and the user's own tickets. tickets' `blocks` links have no why, no inheritance and no cycle check, and its parent rollup marks a parent whose children are all cancelled as done (TK-80.2).
- **Decisions**: only tasks/ has them: questions with options, a recommended one and the answer, folded into Chosen (TK-81).
- **Notes**: tasks/ has the user's notes, the planner's replies, `seen`, and notes on a fragment of a description; tickets has comments with replies in its schema that its web never shows, reactions with no route, no read marks, and nothing on a fragment (TK-82).
- **Rules**: tasks/ checks after the fact (`pnpm tasks:check`: the schema, ids, verb-first titles, approval only on items without children, blockers, cycles); tickets' API checks every write (value types, nesting, link owners, transitions), with no rule on titles and no cycle check (TK-80.6).
- **Screens**: the viewer has the list, filters, the feature page, ticket cards, Approve and Cancel, Your decisions, the notes margin and agent chips, and reads everything every 2 seconds; tickets has project boards (a table and a kanban), item pages, All items, settings and the schema diagram, reads a project every 10 seconds, and has none of the plan's controls (TK-87).
- **Agents**: sessions change the files through `edit()`, which has no lock (TK-89); tickets' writes are commands with an id, a version check and an event, but its MCP server is broken (TK-83); agent reports live only in the viewer (TK-84).
- **Only tickets has**: history (events and an activity feed), configurable types, fields and workflows, saved views, rich text with mentions and images, and safe retries. Neither has sign-in or permissions.

The order: the plans' shape in tickets (TK-80 to TK-82), sign-in (TK-91, before approval and answers), a working MCP server (TK-83), agent reports (TK-84) and projects' repositories (TK-92) can start now; then the import, and an export of the same JSON (TK-85); then the viewer, the planner and the builder move onto tickets' API, the viewer's page unchanged (TK-86); then tickets' own screens, once bh's views reach it (TK-87, after TK-78); last, the viewer and the files go (TK-88). Until the switch the files are still the plan, and TK-89 keeps their edits from being lost. It builds on E4 to E7 rather than repeating them: the items resource (TK-13), templates and views (TK-79, TK-16, TK-19) and the `FilterForm` (TK-75).

plan.title: Add a `plan` scheme: epic, feature, ticket and subticket, with the plans' fields
plan.description:
Seeded like the software scheme (`packages/db/src/seed/software-scheme.ts`). An epic holds features, a feature tickets, a ticket subtickets, and a subticket subtickets of its own.

- A feature's status is a workflow field with the plans' six (Not planned, Planning, Planned, Designed, In progress, Done) and Cancelled, of kind dropped; a ticket's is To do, Done and Cancelled. Restore returns an item to the status it had before it was cancelled (the `from` of the change that cancelled it).
- Text fields, in markdown: description, statusNote, today, stays, rule, chosen and design; chosenOn, a date; waitingOn, text, several.
- `where`: json, `[{repo, part}]` in order, with the repos it names kept in step in a multi-option `repos` field, so a list filters and groups by repo.
- The user's own tickets (`byYou`): assigned to a human user. The builder leaves an item assigned to a human alone.

plan.title: Fix `parent-rollup` setting a parent to done when all its children are cancelled
plan.description: The automation sets a parent to its first done option once every child is done or dropped (`apps/api/src/automation/rules/parent-rollup.ts:50`), so a feature whose tickets are all cancelled becomes Done. The plans' rule is the other way (`scripts/tasks-check.mjs:113`): a parent becomes dropped when every child is dropped, and done when every child is done or dropped and at least one is done. The software scheme gains too: a task whose subtasks are all won't-fix isn't done.

plan.title: Add approval: stored on items without children, worked out for parents
plan.description:
`approved`, a system boolean field that only the `item.approve` command writes (`item.update` refuses it). Approving an item sets it on every item without children under it that isn't done or cancelled, as the viewer's Approve does (`scripts/tasks-view.mjs:84`); taking it back clears them all. Only a signed-in person may approve or take an approval back: the command refuses an agent's token (TK-91).

The API never stores it on an item with children: when an approved item gets its first child, its approval is cleared, and the new children wait for the user's. A parent is approved when an open item is under it and every open one is approved (TK-80.7). Events say who approved what, and when.

They act as the `automation` agent user the worker already creates (`apps/api/src/outbox/worker.ts:85`). Older ticket: TIX-116.

plan.title: Run the stored rules from the outbox worker, one run per event and rule
plan.description: The worker (`apps/api/src/outbox/worker.ts`) already claims events with a lease, retries each up to 5 times and stops at the depth cap, but runs only the code-defined automations. It now also finds each event's matching rules and writes one `rule_executions` row per rule (skipped, with its reason, past the depth cap), then runs the due ones with backoff, reclaiming runs left `running`. A rule never fires on an event its own run caused. Older ticket: TIX-117.

plan.title: Add the rules API: list, create, change and delete rules, and list their runs
plan.description: Routes checked with valibot: `GET` and `POST /api/projects/:key/rules`, `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/rules/:id`, `GET /api/rules/:id/executions` and `GET /api/projects/:key/rule-executions`. A rule's trigger must be a known event kind, its conditions known fields and operators, and its actions well formed for their type. Writes go through commands, as the other config writes do (`apps/api/src/command/config/`). Older ticket: TIX-118.

plan.title: Test rules end to end: a run that works, one that fails, and a loop the depth cap stops
plan.description: On the running stack: make a rule, change an item, and see the action land and its run logged; an illegal `change_status` (failed, logged); a rule that triggers itself (one run); two rules that trigger each other (skipped at the depth cap). Then document the routes in `docs/api/` and the rules in CLAUDE.md. Older ticket: TIX-119.

features.title: Add automation rules that people set up: when an event happens, if its conditions hold, run actions
features.description: Rules stored as data, per project: a trigger (an item event), conditions that must all hold, and actions run in order as the `automation` user. tickets already has the runtime they need: every write is a command whose events carry `depth` and `causedBy` (`packages/db/src/schema/events.ts:29`), the outbox worker drains them at least once and stops at a depth of 8 (`apps/api/src/outbox/worker.ts`, `apps/api/src/automation/constants.ts`), and three automations are written in code (`apps/api/src/automation/rules/`). What's missing is rules stored as data, their runs, and an API to manage them. The July design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-07-automation-event-bus-and-rules-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-07-automation-event-bus-and-rules.md`) predates the items platform: keep its rule model and run log, and use the outbox in place of the event bus it designed. Older ticket: TIX-109.

plan.title: Add the web hooks and types for rules and their runs
plan.description: `useRules`, `useCreateRule`, `useUpdateRule`, `useDeleteRule` and `useRuleExecutions`, with the `AutomationRule`, `RuleCondition`, `RuleAction` and `RuleExecution` types in `apps/web/src/api/types.ts`; writes go through `apiMutate`, as the admin hooks do (`apps/web/src/api/use-admin.ts`). Older ticket: TIX-120.

plan.title: Build the trigger, condition, action and run-status chips
plan.description: Four small read-only chips for the rules list and the runs log: a trigger (an icon and a label for each event kind); a condition (`Type is Bug`, `Status → Done`, `Priority is any of High, Critical`, with "+N more" when they don't fit); an action (`+ Comment`, `Set priority`, `→ Done`, `Webhook`); and a run's status in semantic colors (done positive, failed danger, skipped muted, pending and running neutral) with an attempt count (`failed · 3/5`). Older ticket: TIX-121, TIX-122, TIX-123, TIX-124.

plan.title: Build the builder row for a rule's conditions and actions
plan.description: The repeatable inline row at the heart of the rule editor: selects and inputs side by side, a remove (×), and "+ Add condition" or "+ Add action" below; dense, and usable from the keyboard. The connections' field mapping reuses it. Older ticket: TIX-125.

plan.title: Add the Automations list to Settings
plan.description: A project's rules under a new project item in Settings: each rule's name, trigger chip, condition and action chips, an enable switch (bh's `Switch`), its last run's status, and a row menu to edit or delete it; "+ New rule"; an empty state. Older ticket: TIX-127.

plan.title: Add the rule editor: a drawer of When, If and Then
plan.description: A right-side drawer: name and enable; the trigger (When); condition rows joined by AND (If); action rows with each type's settings and token chips for comment templates (Then); validation, and new and edit states. Older ticket: TIX-128.

plan.title: Add the runs log: every run of a project's rules
plan.description: A table of runs: the rule, the item, the status chip with attempts, the error and the time; filters by rule and status; a run's detail with each action's outcome; an empty state. It shows all five statuses, among them a run failed on an illegal status change and one skipped at the depth cap. Older ticket: TIX-129.

plan.title: Make the Automations screens work at phone width
plan.description: Rules as stacked cards, the rule editor as a full-screen sheet with its builder rows reflowed, and runs as a stacked list with the status first (`docs/design/AutoMobile.dc.html`, `docs/design/07-mobile-interactions.html`). Older ticket: TIX-130.

features.title: Add the Automations screens to Settings: the rules list, the rule editor and the runs log
features.description: The web side of the automation rules, from the Instrument design: `docs/design/08-automations.html`, with `RuleEditor.dc.html`, `RunsLog.dc.html`, `ListShell.dc.html`, `EmptyState.dc.html` and `AutoMobile.dc.html` beside it (the claude.ai design project's `08 Automations`), and the prompt `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-automations-ui-design-prompt.md`. Each part and screen goes through mapping-component-states, implementing-a-component and verifying-a-component, and is built in `apps/web` from bh's parts. It needs the rules API first. Older ticket: TIX-110.

plan.title: Define the connector interface, and store connections with encrypted secrets
plan.description: The `Connector` contract (push, parseInbound, mapFields, configSchema, auth) and a registry of connectors in code. Tables `connections` (project, connector key, name, config, enabled) and `connection_secrets` (encrypted, never sent back by the API). Older ticket: TIX-131.

plan.title: Add the generic HTTP connector, outbound, with a guard against requests to internal addresses
plan.description: Outbound request templates (method, URL, body) using the rules' `{{…}}` tokens; API-key and bearer auth (OAuth later). It pushes changes to mapped items from the event stream, reusing the rule runs' retries and backoff. The guard: a host allowlist, internal and cloud-metadata addresses blocked, timeouts and size caps. Older ticket: TIX-132.

plan.title: Add a Linear connector, outbound
plan.description: Prove the interface with one real code connector: auth, creating and updating an issue, and field mapping. It sets the pattern for Jira and Notion. Older ticket: TIX-133.

plan.title: Build the connection parts: provider card, status chip, masked secret input, auth picker, mapping row and request template editor
plan.description: The parts the connections screens need. The request template editor has token chips and a Send test button; the mapping row reuses the rule editor's builder row. Older ticket: TIX-134.

plan.title: Add the Connections screens: list, provider picker, editors and detail
plan.description: Under workspace settings: the connections list; a provider picker to add one; the editor for a built-in connector (Jira, Linear, Notion); the Custom (HTTP) editor (auth, base URL with its safety note, outbound request templates, field and id mapping, a placeholder for inbound); and a connection's detail with its sync activity, reusing the run-status chip. Secrets are always masked. Older ticket: TIX-135.

features.title: Add connections to outside services: one connector interface, a generic HTTP connector and Linear
features.description: Layer 3 of the July automation roadmap. One `Connector` contract, with a connector (the kind) kept apart from a connection (an instance with its settings and secrets). Two ways to add one: a no-code HTTP connector set up in the web for any REST API, outbound first, and first-party code connectors (Linear first, then Jira or Notion). Connections push outbound from the item events the outbox worker drains, so they come after the automation rules. Designs: `docs/design/09-connections.html`, with `Connections`, `ConnList`, `ConnGallery`, `ConnEmpty`, `ProviderPicker`, `BuiltinEditor` and `CustomEditor` (`.dc.html`) beside it; prompt `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-connections-ui-design-prompt.md`. Older ticket: TIX-111.

plan.title: Add inbound webhooks, verified with a shared secret
plan.description: `/api/connections/:id/inbound` checks each payload's HMAC against the connection's secret, runs the connector's `parseInbound`, and applies the change to the local item as the connection's user, through the same commands as every other write. Older ticket: TIX-136.

plan.title: Link local items to outside objects, and stop echoing a change back
plan.description: `external_links` (connection, local item, external id, last synced hash; unique on connection and external id, and on connection and item) maps each item to its outside object. A change that came in must not be pushed straight back out: compare hashes or the actor. Older ticket: TIX-137.

plan.title: Add detecting and resolving sync conflicts
plan.description: When the local item and the outside object both changed since the last sync (by version or updatedAt), resolve by last writer wins or field by field, and record the conflict so the web can show it. A `sync_conflicts` table was sketched in July: the link, the field, the local and remote values, the resolution, when it was detected and when resolved. Older ticket: TIX-138.

plan.title: Show sync status and conflicts on a connection
plan.description: On a connection's detail: sync activity, direction and when it last synced; a list of conflicts to resolve. Reuses the run-status chip; the design prompt's Sync and Conflicts section (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-connections-ui-design-prompt.md`). Older ticket: TIX-139.

features.title: Add two-way sync with connected services: inbound webhooks, id mapping, echo suppression and conflicts
features.description: Layer 4 of the July automation roadmap, on top of the connectors (the generic HTTP one and code ones alike): changes made outside come in, and a change that came in isn't sent straight back out. The hardest layer; it needs the rules and the connectors first. Older ticket: TIX-112.

plan.title: Add Calendar to a view's modes, with the date field it places items by
plan.description: A view in calendar mode keeps its date field and the fields its chips show; the date-field picker offers only date fields. Older ticket: TIX-170.

plan.title: Build the month and week grid, with a bucket for items without the date
plan.description: Items on their day, "+N more" when a day overflows, and the items with no date in a bucket of their own. Older ticket: TIX-171.

plan.title: Add chips in the day cells, and drag to reschedule
plan.description: A chip shows the view's chosen fields and opens the item when clicked; dragging it to another day writes its date field, only where the field can be written. Older ticket: TIX-172.

plan.title: Show the calendar as an agenda list at phone width
plan.description: Items grouped by date in a list, with the same date field and chips. Older ticket: TIX-173.

features.title: Add a calendar view: items on a month or week grid by a date field
features.description: A new way to show a view: each item on the day of a chosen date field, moved to another day by dragging. Chosen in July: one date per item (no ranges), month and week, drag to reschedule, and an agenda list on a phone. Planned as E5 in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-08-configurable-views-roadmap.md` and drawn as `03b Calendar` in the claude.ai design project a75bdf6d. Views are being redone as JSON in `@bh/view` (TK-16), so the calendar is a host there or a mode of tickets' board, its chips tile templates (TK-79). The software scheme has one date field, `target_date` (`packages/db/src/seed/software-scheme.ts:73`). Older ticket: TIX-145.

plan.title: Add Timeline to a view's modes, with its start, end and row-group fields
plan.description: The start and end pickers offer only date fields; the zoom (week or month) is kept with the view. Older ticket: TIX-174.

plan.title: Build the time axis and the bars, with week and month zoom and a today line
plan.description: One bar per item from its start date to its end date, on an axis that zooms between weeks and months, with a line marking today. Older ticket: TIX-175.

plan.title: Add collapsible row groups, and color bars by status or a chosen field
plan.description: Rows grouped by the chosen field under headers that collapse; bars colored by status group or by a field the view picks. Older ticket: TIX-176.

plan.title: Let bars be dragged and resized to change their dates, and hint at dependencies
plan.description: Dragging a bar moves both dates and dragging an edge moves one, only where the fields can be written. A dashed line joins items a blocking link connects, found by what the link type means rather than its key `blocks`. Older ticket: TIX-177.

features.title: Add a timeline view: bars from a start date to an end date
features.description: A horizontal time axis with a bar per item, from a start date field to an end date field, rows grouped by a chosen field. Chosen in July: bars can be dragged and resized, and dependencies are only a hint. Planned as E6 in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-08-configurable-views-roadmap.md` and drawn as `03c Timeline` in the claude.ai design project a75bdf6d; like the calendar, it's a host or a mode on the views of TK-16. The software scheme has only one date field (`target_date`, `packages/db/src/seed/software-scheme.ts:73`), so a timeline needs a start date field as well. Older ticket: TIX-146.

plan.title: Add grouping kanban columns by any option or user field
plan.description: Grouped by status, a drop keeps to the workflow's legal moves (`apps/web/src/utils/legal-status-targets.ts`); grouped by another field, a drop sets that field's value. Get this rule right once, in `apps/web/src/components/kanban-view.tsx` or what replaces it (TK-22). Older ticket: TIX-163.

plan.title: Add swimlanes and WIP limits to the kanban board
plan.description: A second grouping draws horizontal lanes, each with a header and a count; a column may have a work-in-progress limit and shows when it's over it. Older ticket: TIX-164.

plan.title: Add Save and Reset for a view's unsaved changes
plan.description: Changes to a view's columns, sort, grouping and filters stay a draft, marked unsaved, until Save writes them to the view or Reset drops them, in place of saving each change as it's made (`apps/web/src/state/use-view-config.ts:53`). The board already keeps unsaved filters in the address until they're saved, and All items shows an unsaved dot with Reset. Older ticket: TIX-157.

features.title: Add to board views: kanban grouping by any field, swimlanes, WIP limits, and Save and Reset for changes
features.description: Three choices from the July views plan that the views rework (TK-16 to TK-22) leaves out: TK-22.1 builds kanban columns from status groups only, nothing adds lanes or limits, and TK-16.4 stores a reader's changes per view where July chose a draft that Save writes to the view. The rest of the July board work is planned: cards from a tile template (TK-22.2) and their editor (TK-20.2). Older ticket: TIX-143.

plan.title: Add editing a comment, and Edit and Delete on an item's comments
plan.description: Deleting is built on branch `tk-82` (TK-82.4: `DELETE /api/comments/:id`, by its author only, setting `deleted_at` and emitting `comment.deleted`). Add `PATCH /api/comments/:id` for its author to change the body, emitting `comment.edited`; Edit and Delete on each comment in the web (`apps/web/src/components/detail-comments.tsx`); and matching MCP tools once the MCP server works again (TK-83.1). Older ticket: TIX-86.

plan.title: Add moving an item to another project
plan.description: Today an item can only be copied and the original archived, which loses its id, its events and its comments. A move keeps the item's row, so they follow it. The item takes the next number in the target project, with its old key kept visible (or kept outright, if TK-80.3's stored key allows); its children move with it. Projects on the same scheme share types, fields and options, so only a move between schemes needs a remap by key, with a rule for a key the target lacks (refuse it, or create it). Links stay, since the API already lets a link cross projects (`apps/api/src/command/item/link.ts`). Older ticket: TIX-80.

plan.title: Add archiving a project, and deleting one with no items
plan.description: Projects can only be created and renamed (`apps/api/src/command/config/project.ts`). Add `archived_at` to `core.projects` (in the model, `packages/db/src/schema/items-platform.json`, as well as drizzle), a `project.archive` command that hides the project from the list by default, and a delete for a project with no items that removes it and its views in one transaction. An Archive action in the web, and an MCP tool beside `list_projects`. Older ticket: TIX-87.

plan.title: Delete the DEMO project from the live and dev databases
plan.description: The seeded `demo` project (prefix DEMO), a smoke test from the July Docker setup, still sits beside the real projects in the live database with 2 archived items (`Projects/tickets-backups/2026-10-13-older-projects/SUMMARY.md`, TK-85.1), and is in that backup. Remove it with the project delete above, or along with the older projects (TK-85.7 on the dev database, TK-85.8 on the live one), which remove items with their values, comments, links and events. Older ticket: TIX-79, TIX-85.

features.title: Add editing comments, moving items between projects, and archiving and deleting projects
features.description: Writes the API and the web still lack, each found in July when a fix had to be made by hand in SQL. Older ticket: TIX-104.

plan.title: Add managing an option field's options in Settings
plan.description: The API adds, renames, reorders and archives options on any option field (`POST /api/fields/:id/options`, `PATCH /api/options/:id`), but the web does it only for the workflow's statuses (`apps/web/src/components/settings/workflow-tab.tsx:186`). A field made in Settings → Fields with type `option` gets an empty option set (`apps/api/src/command/config/field.ts:29`) and no way to fill it. Add an options editor to the Fields tab. Older ticket: TIX-151.

plan.title: Replace the item screens' fixed `title`, `description`, `blocks` and `subtask` keys with what the scheme says
plan.description: The detail reads `values['title']` and a field keyed `description` (`apps/web/src/components/item-detail.tsx:119`, `:126`), marks a link as blocking only when its key is `blocks` (`detail-links.tsx:24`), and adds children as type `subtask` (`detail-children.tsx:151`, `new-item-dialog.tsx:25`). The plan scheme's child type is `subticket` (branch `tk-80`, `packages/db/src/seed/plan-scheme.ts`), so "Add subtask" finds no type there. Find the title and description by their role with a fallback, a blocking link by what its link type means, and the child type from the parent type's allowed children (`structure.item_type_child_types`): that part is TK-80.12, needed for the plans first. Older ticket: TIX-180. Left after TK-80.12 (2026-10-14): the children section's header still says "Subtasks" on a plan feature or ticket (only its add row is named by type); the New item picker still treats `subtask` as special by key (`creatableTypes`, its disabled row, `SUBTASK_KEY` in `new-item-dialog.tsx`) and offers a plan's ticket and subticket at the top level, which the API refuses without a parent; and `SubtaskQuickCreate` (`new-item-dialog.tsx`) is exported but used only by tests, so it goes.

features.title: Make Settings and the item screens work with any scheme, not only the software one
features.description: Two places where the web assumes the seeded software scheme. Both matter more now that a plan scheme (TK-80.1) sits beside it. Older ticket: TIX-151, TIX-180.

features.title: Update the API and MCP docs pages to today's routes
features.description: Eight pages in `docs/api` and `docs/mcp` still describe the old `/api/tickets` routes, which were replaced by `/api/items` and the project routes. Found while triaging the older TIX tickets; no ticket asked for it.
